title: A Escarpment for the Trail
premise: Hazel Okonkwo, a bush pilot ferrying medicine and gossip across the interior, accepts a hand-drawn map from a dying prospector in exchange for a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter. The map points to the source of the Kestrel River, a headwater hidden inside a mining concession whose permits expire in thirty days — and whose owner, Silas Vane, will do anything to keep what lies there buried. Flying upriver with the prospector's daughter, Ruth, Hazel discovers that the 'forbidden source' is not gold but evidence of a decades-old massacre Vane's company committed and covered up, proof that could void every permit he holds. Hunted by Vane's enforcers through rapids, fire, and fog, Hazel must choose between flying home safe and staying to carry the truth out on foot. In the end she crashes her plane deliberately to block the company's last supply run, survives the escarpment descent with Ruth, and delivers the testimony that strips Vane of his empire — finding, at last, that belonging is something you build by what you refuse to abandon.
about_author: Rafael Winterbourne is a former floatplane mechanic who spent six years in remote northern camps before turning to writing full-time. His fiction draws on the pilots, prospectors, and quiet liars he met along the rivers, and on his conviction that wilderness is less cruel than the men who claim to own it.

chapters.title: Freight and Rumor
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. A routine medicine run into the interior introduces Hazel's world: her battered de Havilland, the scattered communities she serves, and the growing presence of Vane Consolidated's survey crews along the Kestrel. She overhears rumors of a prospector hiding out upstream. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness — Hazel belongs to the sky but no place below it.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. At a trapper's cabin, Hazel finds Eben Crowe, a prospector dying of a burst ulcer, who trades her a grease-pencil map for a promise: take it to his daughter Ruth in Fort Meridian before the concession permits lapse. He whispers that the river's source 'remembers what Vane paid to forget.' Emotional beat: the weight of a promise made to a stranger's ghost.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. In Fort Meridian, Hazel finds Ruth Crowe — hard, skeptical, estranged from the father who chose rivers over her. Ruth refuses the map until Vane's men arrive asking pointed questions about Eben, confirming there is something worth killing for. Emotional beat: two guarded women recognizing the same wound in each other.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth deciphers her father's map while Hazel charts the route; they learn the permits expire in a month, after which Vane's claim — and whatever he's hiding — becomes untouchable. They commit to going upriver together. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose; the first fragile trust between them.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel flies them to a lakehead and they travel by canoe through country Vane's crews are stripping bare. They find Eben's old camp ransacked and a surveyor's cache revealing drill cores sealed under confidentiality orders. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the scale of Vane's operation becomes clear.

chapters.title: The Escarpment
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Portaging toward the escarpment wall that guards the headwater, they spot Vane's enforcer, Callum Reeve, tracking them. A near-capture in the fog forces them to abandon their heaviest gear. Ruth confesses her father wrote to her every year and she never answered. Emotional beat: grief and guilt laid open under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Source Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Above the falls they find the source: an abandoned settlement, unmarked graves, and Eben's sealed field journals documenting the 1971 massacre of striking workers that founded Vane's fortune. Reeve ambushes them; they escape with the journals but Hazel's plane, parked at the lakehead, is their only way out. Emotional beat: horror and terrible clarity — the map was never about treasure.

chapters.title: Reeve's River
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Hunted downriver by Reeve and Vane's hired crew, the women run white water at night, lose their canoe in a gorge, and survive on Ruth's father's old survival caches — his letters to her hidden inside, years of unanswered love. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the dead father through the landscape he loved.

chapters.title: The Last Supply Run
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Cornered at the lakehead with Vane arriving by barge to destroy the evidence before the permits lapse, Hazel makes her choice: she flies her plane into the barge's fuel depot, stranding Vane's operation past the deadline and destroying her own livelihood in the blast. Emotional beat: sacrifice as identity — Hazel finally belongs somewhere by burning her escape route.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: POV Hazel and Ruth alternating. Weeks later, the journals reach a journalist and a tribunal; Vane's permits are revoked and investigations begin. Hazel, grounded and broke, takes work running the river mail route by canoe with Ruth beside her. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — power stripped of its corruption, and two women who found belonging not in a place, but in each other and the truth they carried out.
